key_insight: Quantile-based distributional reinforcement learning can estimate return distributions with statistically efficient, root-n accurate inference, even as the number of quantiles grows.
engineering_relevance: This provides a principled and sample-efficient way to evaluate policies in RL systems when uncertainty over returns matters, such as in risk-sensitive or safety-critical decision making.
method: Build a finite-dimensional return-distribution representation using the quantile-projected Bellman fixed point.
Construct an empirical MDP estimator from a generative model and analyze its non-asymptotic sup-W∞ error.
Derive asymptotic normality, semiparametric efficiency, and Berry–Esseen guarantees for quantile functionals.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a non-asymptotic error rate of \u007eO(\u221a(m/n)) and shows the estimator attains the semiparametric efficiency bound.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on access to a generative model and fixed-policy evaluation, so performance may differ in offline or interactive RL settings with limited sampling.
paper_title: Statistical Efficiency and Inference of Quantile Distributional Reinforcement Learning
